messages:
julia: Quick sync — thinking about how service-to-service delegation should surface tenant claims when requests hop through a proxy. Example: frontend -> auth-proxy -> inference. We need to avoid leaking tenant ids to unrelated downstreams but still preserve authz checks. Thoughts?

sangeeta: +1. Two obvious patterns: 1) full chain in JWT (signed chain entries) 2) opaque reference to a chain stored in auth service. Both have pros/cons.

ryan: Full chain is easiest for offline checks (no roundtrip) but token size and leaking info to third parties is a real risk. Also makes token replay surface larger attack surface.

omar: For regulated tenants we can't leak tenant metadata beyond what the downstream needs. So principle: least-privilege claims by default.

julia: sketch idea: frontend mints short-lived JWT (user sub), auth-proxy validates and issues a new token with {sub, actor_chain: ["user:123","svc:auth-proxy"]} signed by proxy key. Downstream services verify proxied token and consult actor_chain for audit. Problem: chain grows and inflates token size.

sangeeta: alternative: token reference pattern — proxy stores chain in auth datastore and issues opaque token like: {ref: "tk_abc", aud: "inference", exp: ...}. Downstream calls auth introspect endpoint or a cached lookup to resolve chain when needed.

ryan: reference pattern reduces token bloat and avoids leaking tenant ids in the header, but adds runtime coupling and latency (introspect call) and creates availability concerns for high-throughput inference paths.

julia: tradeoff matrix we should consider: privacy (leakage), latency (introspect cost), availability (auth store), auditability (where chain is stored), token verification complexity (cross-signing), and caching behavior.

omar: caching helps. If inference nodes cache resolved refs with TTL tuned to token expiry, introspect calls are rare. But cache invalidation on revocation is tricky.

sangeeta: proposal: hybrid approach — include a compact digest of the actor chain in the token (e.g., chain_hash) + opaque ref to full chain stored in auth. Downstream can verify chain integrity by checking digest against resolved chain when they need full context; otherwise they make decisions based on minimal claims in the token.

ryan: I like the digest + ref. It gives quick local verification that the chain hasn't been tampered with if they ever fetch it later. For pure allow/deny checks you can use the minimal claims.

julia: implementation notes:
```
Header: X-RW-Actor-Ref: tk_abc123
Payload: {sub: "user:123", tenant: "t:acme", aud: "inference", chain_hash: "sha256:...", exp: 1690000000}
```
Auth store record: {ref: "tk_abc123", chain: ["user:123","svc:auth-proxy"], signatures: [...], created_by: "auth-proxy"}

omar: security questions: who can resolve refs? internal-only endpoints with mTLS. Make sure the introspect endpoint requires caller identity and logs resolution events for audit.

sangeeta: also consider short TTLs for refs + push-revocation signals (pub/sub) to invalidate caches if a token is revoked. We should avoid polling.

ryan: perf: for high-throughput non-sensitive calls we can short-circuit and rely on cached minimal claims. For high-sensitivity flows we fetch full chain and validate signatures. That gives SLO tradeoff knobs.

julia: compatibility: SDKs should surface helpers to store/resolve refs and fallback to introspect transparently. Console should show chain when expanded.

omar: ops: we'll need metrics: introspect latency, cache hit-rate, resolve rate per tenant, revocation events. Also rate-limit introspect.

devops-bot: scheduled: auth-store-rotation job will run nightly at 03:00 UTC to rotate introspect keys.

sangeeta: next step: write short RFC that proposes digest+ref pattern, enumerates threat model, revocation model, and runtime caching rules. We should include sample headers and an introspect API shape.

ryan: I can prototype an in-memory resolver with cache and revocation hook for perf tests.

julia: I'll draft the RFC and include the decision matrix + examples. Assign owners: julia (RFC), ryan (prototype), sangeeta (security review), omar (ops + metrics).

omar: one more: consider optional redaction for third-party plugins — when a request includes plugin-aud scope, we strip tenant id and only pass ephemeral plugin-scoped creds. We'll capture as a followup in the RFC.

julia: great — I'll drop the RFC link here when ready and we can review next week. :+1:
